transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since they changed my position at the shop, I just can’t seem to adjust, and it’s throwing off my work and my whole routine. I'm just finding it really hard to get my bearings since the restructuring happened.
Have you been experiencing excessive worry or fear about your new role or work performance since the change?

Yes, I've been dealing with this constant mix of dread and defeat, and I feel so wound up about the new role since the transition. I'm really worried about my performance, especially since my new supervisor already pulled me aside about my slipping numbers and missing some deadlines.
Did your feelings of dread, defeat, and worry start immediately after the change in your job position or did they develop gradually over time after the transition?

They actually started pretty quickly, within a week or two of being switched to the new position and supervisor. Since then, those feelings of dread and defeat have just steadily worsened over the last month instead of settling down.
Have you experienced any significant traumatic event or extreme stressor in your life recently, aside from the job change, that you think might be contributing to how you're feeling?

No, there hasn't been anything else like that. My life, my routines, and my art sculptures were all going really well until this sudden job restructuring happened last month. This workplace change is the sole reason I've been feeling so thrown off and defeated.
Can you describe if your feelings of dread and defeat are specifically focused on the new job role and performance, or if they have started to affect other areas of your life beyond work?

They've definitely spilled over into my personal life; I go home so exhausted and defeated that I just sit on the couch staring at my unfinished metal sculptures. I've stopped doing things I love like paddle-boarding and pickleball, and I'm falling behind on my art commissions and cancelling on friends. It's really starting to disrupt my household and hurt my reputation.

Are you experiencing these feelings of dread, defeat, and worry primarily when you're at work or thinking about work, or have they become more pervasive and started to affect your relationships with friends and family as well?

They’ve definitely become more pervasive and are affecting my relationships outside of work. I find myself snapping at people and backing out of plans with friends, and my spouse has really noticed how much this is disrupting our household routine.
Can you tell me more about how your relationships with your spouse and friends have changed since you started feeling this way, and if they've noticed any difference in your behavior or mood?

My spouse has definitely noticed the change and points out how much this job shift has disrupted our household schedule and my daily functioning. I come home so wound up and defeated that I end up snapping at people or just staring at the couch, and I've been backing out of plans with my friends lately.

Have you experienced any significant avoidance behaviors, such as avoiding certain tasks or situations at work, or avoiding social interactions with friends and family, as a way of coping with your feelings of dread and defeat?

Yes, I've definitely been avoiding social interactions and my usual activities. I've backed out of plans with my friends for paddle-boarding and pickleball, and I'm avoiding working on my commissioned metal sculptures. Most nights, I just sit on the couch feeling too exhausted and defeated to do anything I used to enjoy.

You mentioned you've stopped doing things you love like paddle-boarding, pickleball, and working on your metal sculptures. Are you finding that you're no longer enjoying these activities or is it more that you're just not having the energy to participate in them?

It’s really a mix of both, but mostly I’m just too wound up, exhausted, and defeated after work to even try. Instead of enjoying my hobbies, I end up just sitting on the couch staring at my half-finished sculpture. I just don't have the drive or the peace of mind to actually participate in them right now.

Do you think if your work situation improved or the stress from the job change was removed, you would regain your interest and enjoyment in activities like paddle-boarding, pickleball, and working on your metal sculptures?

Yes, definitely. If they moved me back to my old team or eased up on these quotas, I feel like I could get back to my normal routine and enjoy sculpting, paddle-boarding, and pickleball again within a few months. Right now I just feel stuck, but removing that work stress would make a huge difference.

Can you tell me if there are any specific times or situations when your feelings of dread, defeat, and worry are significantly worse, such as when you're at work, thinking about work, or when you're trying to fall asleep?

They are definitely at their worst during the workday when I'm struggling to meet those repetitive quotas under my new supervisor. It also hits me really hard the moment I get home, where I'm just too wound up and defeated to do anything but stare at my unfinished sculptures.

Do you think you would still be experiencing these feelings of dread, defeat, and worry if you were not in this new work situation, or do you believe they would resolve on their own without any changes to your job?

I definitely wouldn't be feeling this way if it weren't for this new job situation. I really believe that if they moved me back to my old team or eased up on the quotas, I could get back to my normal routine and feel like myself again within a few months. Right now, I just feel completely stuck because of how things are at the shop.

You've mentioned that your feelings of dread and defeat are primarily related to your new job situation, but can you think of any other significant life changes or stressors that might be contributing to your emotional state, even if they seem unrelated to your job?

No, there really isn't anything else going on in my life. Before this sudden restructuring at the shop, my home life, my art commissions, and my daily routines were all completely stable and fulfilling. Everything I'm struggling with right now stems directly from this workplace change.
Have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, or hopelessness that are not just limited to your work situation or daily frustrations?

I wouldn't say it's a general sadness; these feelings of being on the verge of tears and defeat are directly tied to the sudden job restructuring and how it has disrupted my routine and passion for sculpting. If it weren't for the stress and changes at work, I really don't think I would be feeling this way at all. It all comes back to what's happening at the shop.
Have you experienced any moments of intense emotional reactivity, such as sudden outbursts of anger or tears, in response to relatively minor stressors or reminders of your job situation?

Yes, ever since they stuck me on this new line, I feel like I’m constantly on the verge of tears or snapping at people. I go home feeling incredibly wound up and defeated, and it really doesn't take much to set me off lately.
Can you describe how you typically cope with stressful situations, and if there's been a change in your ability to manage stress since the job change occurred?

Normally, I cope with stress through creative and active outlets like my metal sculpting, paddle-boarding, and pickleball. Since the job change, my ability to manage stress has completely broken down. Now, I just cancel plans, let my art sit unfinished, and find myself sitting on the couch feeling exhausted and defeated instead of doing the things that used to help me recharge.
Have you been experiencing any persistent feelings of worthlessness or guilt that are not just related to your job performance, but rather a general feeling about yourself?

No, I don't really feel a general sense of worthlessness or guilt about myself as a person. My feelings of defeat and frustration are specifically tied to these job changes and falling behind on my work and art. Outside of this situation, I don't have those constant, general feelings about myself.

You mentioned that you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, such as paddle-boarding and working on your metal sculptures. Can you tell me if there's been a complete loss of pleasure in these activities or if you still feel some enjoyment when you do manage to participate in them?

I haven't actually been participating in those activities at all lately because when I get home, I feel too wound up and defeated to even start. Looking at my half-finished sculptures or thinking about paddle-boarding just makes me feel stressed and guilty about falling behind. It doesn't bring me any pleasure right now; it just adds to the pressure.

If the stress from your job situation were completely removed, do you think your mood and interest in activities would return to normal, or do you think you would still experience some persistent feelings of sadness or loss of interest?

Yes, I absolutely believe my mood and interest would return to normal if the job stress were resolved. If they moved me back to my old fabrication team or eased up on these quotas, I feel confident I'd get back to my normal routine and passion for metal sculpting within a few months instead of feeling so stuck.
